events.title: Global transition away from oil could trigger conflict, migration, and economic upheaval
events.one_liner: Researchers warn that the global energy transition away from oil risks triggering conflict, migration, and economic instability in oil-dependent nations without urgent government intervention. Countries like Nigeria, Iran, Angola, and Algeria face severe risk due to heavy revenue dependence and limited economic diversification, as oil demand plateaus in the early 2030s.
takeaways: Oil demand forecast to plateau in early 2030s, forcing producer competition
Nigeria, Iran, Angola, Algeria face severe risk from oil revenue dependence and low diversification
Cheapest producers (Saudi Arabia, UAE) likely to outcompete others with weak infrastructure
Venezuela cited as cautionary example of state collapse from oil dependence
Report published September 8, 2026 by E3G thinktank
